data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient because it can dynamically isolate and evacuate traffic from failing segments faster than a decentralized network can adapt.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The failure is caused by the control plane itself, making the 'evacuation' mechanism the primary vector of collapse.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'poison pill' is passed along with the traffic, causing every segment the traffic is shifted to also fail immediately.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Unified observability and a global control plane allow for near-instantaneous traffic shifting (evacuation) away from a detected failure.
